title: Mapping the hidden geography of Earth’s deep mantle using graph theory and AI
text:
Our new study in Science uses graph theory to trace plausible mantle-plume pathways through seismic tomography beneath East Africa and the Indian Ocean. By comparing these pathways with independent geochemicial data with AI-based clustering analysis, we identify at least three compositionally distinct source regions within the African LLSVP and construct the first joint geophysical-geochemical zoning map of the lowermost mantle in this region.



Earth cut open beneath East Africa and the Indian Ocean, from the surface to the core-mantle boundary about 3,000 km below. Orange clouds show seismically slow, plume-like mantle; colored lines show the best plume paths identified using graph theory, connecting hotspot volcanism to deep source regions.





Seven conceptual models are shown from left to right, with their names and example references below.


The work was also covered by Harvard FAS.

title: Call for Papers in Machine Learning and Geosciences
text: PNAS Nexus, the sister journal of PNAS (a gold open-access journal), has announced a call for papers for a special issue on “Machine Learning and Geosciences.” No publication fees will be charged. Submissions are welcome on the application and methodological advancement of machine learning in geosciences. The journal targets a broad scientific audience and encourages interdisciplinary research with wide impact. Accepted papers will be published online on a rolling basis. This special issue will be co-edited by Barbara Romanowicz (UC Berkeley) and Xiyuan Bao (Harvard). The submission deadline is March 15, 2026. To express your interest and obtain submission instructions, please contact the editorial office at pnasnexus.editorialoffice@oup.com. For more details, please refer to this link. We warmly welcome your submissions and would greatly appreciate your help in sharing this call with colleagues.

title: Xiyuan Bao
text:
Xiyuan Bao鲍习源


Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation Postdoctoral Fellow, Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Harvard University


Research: Mantle Dynamics · Surface Processes and Interior–Surface Coupling · Machine Learning in Earth Science


 Email   Google Scholar   ORCID   GitHub   LinkedIn 




Fire and ice: how Earth’s deep interior shapes its surface
I study the coupled dynamics of Earth’s interior and surface, from mantle plumes to sea-level rise, with simulations, experiments and machine learning. I am a Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation Postdoctoral Fellow at Harvard University, with a PhD in geophysics from UCLA.
Learn more on the Research page.

Explore Your Universe, UCLA · 2019–2022

Why is Hawaii a volcano?
Explore Your Universe is the largest public science event in Los Angeles, with over 10,000 visitors each year. Since 2019 I led a booth on hotspots like Hawaii, with hands-on demonstrations using thermochromic liquid crystals and a lava lamp, plus online tutorials for K-12 students and up. The posts are hosted on my PhD group website, which I also built and maintained.

Scientists boarding D/V JOIDES Resolution off New Jersey in 1993. Sea level in an ice-free world would be 66 meters (216.5 feet) higher than now—shoulder-high to the Statue of Liberty. Image credit: Kenneth G. Miller, James V. Browning, and Gregory S. Mountain
